The concern that these two types of shifts could occur arises not only from economic theory about consumer behavior, but also from the experience of the EPA in regulating the emissions in light duty trucks. When emission standards initially became effective for these vehicles, a substantial number of them were slightly less than 6,000 pounds GVWR. Several years later, primarily through manufacturer choice, the rating of these vehicles increased to slightly over 6,000 pounds GVWR. As a result, the vehicles were not classified as light duty trucks, and became subject to the less stringent emissions standards applicable to heavy duty engines. In the EPA rule mentioned above, that agency is proposing to reverse the effect of that shift to heavier vehicles by expanding the light duty truck category to include trucks more than 6,000 pounds GVWR and less than 8,500 pounds GVWR.
